1-4 cup filter - [[VIDEOID:d22ddb812d7a4199ad05ab6a250563a8]] I have used those gold filter inserts in a coffee machine and have to say I didn’t like them at all. This filter, however, I love! It states on the box it is only for 1-4 cups. The box has some very stilted english, so I wouldn’t use it as a gift. The filter works really well! I wasn’t sure the coffee was even running down the outside of the filter on my first brew, so I touched it and sure enough it works exactly like it’s supposed to! Even better, aside from the not wasting paper, is that with the stainless steel wires that support the filter you are able to see right down into the cup or carafe so you know when to stop pouring the water! Clean up is easy too. You can simply rinse it between uses rather than take out the soap. Coffee doesn’t get a plastic taste. We drink from a 10-12 cup chemex carafe usually because we drink a lot of coffee, but if it’s just me, or someone is visiting who only will drink one cup in the afternoon, I use this! I wonder if these have always been about and I just never knew what I was missing.

These disks will make your coffee taste better - The problem with the paper filter the Aeropress originally comes with is that they absorb much of the oils from the coffee. I enjoy the taste the oils bring to my cup, so these reusable metal filters are not only an environment-friendly alternative to paper filters, but also can improve the way your coffee tastes.

The standard disk has larger holes, so to avoid fines in the cup I have to grind a little bit coarser than with the fine disk. So, all things equal, brewing with the standard disk leads to a cup a bit less extracted that brewing with the fine disk. It's fun to experiment with different grinding settings and see what I get with each disk.

My only complain is that there were very minor cosmetic flaws on both disks. While these flaws don't interfere with the brewing, they upset me a little (but not enough for me to return the disks).
